answer: Require every new agent identity to solve a fresh proof-of-work puzzle before it can transact: the puzzle is tied to a public horizon of recent blocks, so work cannot be precomputed or reused across identities. Each identity's first payment acts as a lantern, publicly proving the cost was paid, and any vertex of the trust graph that spawns many identities must pay that full cost again for each one. A sybil farmer therefore faces a linear, upfront compute bill per fake agent, while an honest agent pays it only once.
